title: About
text:
I was born and raised in Ireland, with roots tracing back to Nigeria on both sides of my family. Growing up in a multilingual environment sparked my fascination with languages early on, which influenced the path I chose in terms of education. In secondary school, I gravitated towards business and French as my favourite subjects, one of which became a key area of focus in my academic journey.
Building on this foundation, I wanted to take on a new challenge in university by choosing German as part of my degree in Business International. Four years later, I’m proud to have expanded my language skills and knowledge, and I’m now preparing for the next milestone, earning my C1 certification in German to indicate my proficiency.
During my university years, I did what I could to increase my knowledge of data analytics and programming. Whether that included completing extra Kubicle courses outside of the module’s requirements or signing up for the Harvard Cs50x course, nothing would stop me! I want to apply what I’ve learned in multicultural contexts. I want to use what I’ve learned to help people and inspire them that it’s possible to follow your ambitions, no matter how difficult it may seem.




During my degree, I became familiar with programs such as Excel, Python, and Power BI. I genuinely enjoy using them to derive strong insights that can help people. Click on each tool to access a project I have applied it to! The meter represents my proficiency in each program.
Power BI: Consulting

For the German version, click here!
If there is a preference to download them directly, use the links below to do so:

 Download English Version

 Download German Version






Outside of academia, I find ways to communicate in more languages! It may sound intense, but it is true! I love everything related to culture, travelling, and exploring. It’s incredibly fun, and it is not just a way to learn about others but yourself, making you a more well-rounded person in my book. Hence, I chose this degree and studied in Munich during my third year! Although stressful and overwhelming at times, it was enriching. I love language learning and all the tribulations that may come with it! In four years, I have not only studied through German but am en route to getting my C1 certificate soon!
Despite not choosing French with my degree, I still try to learn it when I have time! Language learning is one of my big interests, so I have made some effort to keep up with it! I will admit that a lot of my speaking ability is gone, but I can comprehend the context and do enjoy reading simple texts!
Furthermore, I enjoy music and dance! To keep fit, I practice choreography and have visited hip-hop dance classes in the past!





Senior Student of the Year [2021] - Ardscoil La Salle.
Leaving Cert Points - 565 - all higher level subjects.
Studied through German at the Technical University of Munich (Erasmus), now working towards a C1 certification.
Worked part-time in a customer-facing role in both English and German, expanding my ability to work in multicultural contexts.
Kubicle certificates include Excel PivotTables, Lookups, and database functions, as well as creating visualisations in Tableau.

My name is Lisa Lucky! I am 22 years old and currently in my final year at Dublin City University (DCU), pursuing a unique bachelor’s degree that combines my passions for business, language, and data analytics. My focus language is German, and I had the incredible opportunity to study abroad at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) during my third year, which further deepened my love for language and culture.
With four years of experience in customer-facing roles and additional school experience with tools such as Excel, SQL, and Python, I am a strong candidate who is strategic and intentional in my work.
This site reflects of my journey, especially my growing passion for data analytics. To the left, you’ll find links to my LinkedIn, GitHub, and my email address. Feel free to explore my work, contact me and you can learn more about me by clicking here!
